comparison: Perfect agreement on recall error findings (C3, C4, C20-C40). Both evaluations rate these claims as SUPPORTED with strong statistical evidence. Reviewers explicitly accepted the 'specific decrease in the precision of VWM recall in MS' that OpenEval also validated.

Perfect agreement on precision findings across paradigms (C41-C56). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers specifically noted the study identifies 'a specific decrease in the precision of VWM recall,' aligning with OpenEval's assessment of consistent statistical evidence.

Perfect agreement on von Mises SD findings (C57-C66). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers praised the 'mixture modelling to disentangle different contributions,' which includes these circular statistics results that OpenEval validated as using appropriate methods.

Partial disagreement on target response and swap error claims. OpenEval rates R4 (C67-C78) as SUPPORTED but notes causal language concerns in R5 (C7-C8, C79-C84). Peer review groups all these claims together (R4) and rates UNCERTAIN due to concerns that 'visual and/or motor impairments contribute to performance decrements' cannot be ruled out, raising broader confound concerns than OpenEval identified.

Disagreement on swap error interpretation (C7, C8, C79-C84). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED despite noting overly causal language. Peer review includes these in their UNCERTAIN evaluation, expressing concern about visual/motor confounds that OpenEval did not emphasize as strongly.

Disagreement on uniform response findings (C85-C89). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN because effects became insignificant after covariate adjustment. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting these as part of the mixture modeling approach without noting the covariate adjustment issue that concerned OpenEval.

Perfect agreement on ROC analysis and discriminative findings (C5, C6, C90-C101). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers found evidence 'convincing' and noted the study 'provides valuable information,' aligning with OpenEval's validation of the classification accuracies and dissociable patterns.

Agreement on uncertainty of mechanistic interpretations. OpenEval rates hippocampal mechanism claims (C102-C106) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct measurement. Peer review rates overlapping speculative claims (C103, C106, C108, C120-C122) as UNCERTAIN, noting visual/motor confounds cannot be ruled out. Both recognize these go beyond the data.

Agreement on uncertainty of neural mechanism claims (C107-C111). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN because no neural activity was directly measured. Peer review includes some of these claims (C108) in their UNCERTAIN evaluation of speculative interpretations, though groups them differently.

Agreement on uncertainty of neuroanatomical interpretations (C112-C121). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative without neuroimaging data. Peer review includes C120-C121 in their UNCERTAIN evaluation, both recognizing these are hypotheses rather than demonstrated findings.

Disagreement on memory load inference (C122). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing it as reasonable inference from the data pattern. Peer review includes this in their UNCERTAIN evaluation of speculative claims, suggesting more caution about this interpretation.

Agreement on participant numbers (C17-C19, C123-C124) as SUPPORTED. Both accept these methodological details, though OpenEval notes unexplained sample size differences between paradigms. Peer review acknowledges 'weaknesses with the way clinical groups were matched' but accepts the framework.

Agreement on methodological details (C125-C130) as SUPPORTED. Both evaluations accept the inclusion/exclusion criteria and ethical compliance as adequately described, with peer reviewers noting acknowledged limitations.

Agreement on background claims (C1, C2, C9-C16) as SUPPORTED. Both accept these as appropriately cited established knowledge. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted by noting the study 'represents an advance beyond prior work,' and OpenEval validated the citations as appropriate.

Partial overlap on background and mechanistic claims. OpenEval rates hippocampal mechanism (C102, C104-C106) as UNCERTAIN. Peer review rates broader background claims including some mechanistic ones (C102, C104, C105 among C1-C119) as SUPPORTED, showing less concern about distinguishing background citations from speculative mechanisms.

Partial overlap on neural mechanism background. OpenEval rates claims about theta oscillations and neural activity (C107, C109-C111) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct measurement. Peer review includes these in broader SUPPORTED background claims (R8), not distinguishing them as speculative.

Partial overlap on neuroanatomical background. OpenEval rates claims about brain regions and networks (C112-C119) as UNCERTAIN speculation. Peer review includes these in SUPPORTED background claims, treating them as established knowledge from citations rather than speculative interpretations requiring caution.
